Frontend: /printout-labels renders with all expected testids (pl-upload-zone, pl-latest-dl-{MASTER_PRINT,TIER1_HIGH_VOLUME,TIER2_LOW_VOLUME}.pdf, pl-reset-btn, pl-date-start/end, pl-preset-today, pl-file-input, pl-process-btn, pl-downloads-panel). Master (2129 bytes) and Tier-2 (2129 bytes) downloads also work. Clicking 'Reset all runs' after confirm zeroes all KPIs and hides the Latest Run panel.
critical_code_review_comments: routers/pdf_sorter.py analytics() uses `Dict[str, Any]` in a runtime annotation but only imports `List, Optional` from typing. It works today only because `from __future__ import annotations` is at the top so annotations are lazily evaluated as strings — but if anyone ever removes that import or converts to a runtime type check (e.g. Pydantic v2 model), it will break with NameError. Low priority nit: add `Dict, Any` to the typing import for safety.

services/pdf_sorter.py TIER1_MIN_PAGES=10 is hard-coded — the frontend labels the button 'Tier 1 · High Volume' but for small test uploads (<10 pages/SKU) EVERYTHING goes to Tier 2 which is easy to mistake for a bug. Consider making the threshold configurable via the pdf_sorter config collection so QA/users can test tier splits without needing 10+ pages of the same SKU.

The download route on GET /runs/{run_id}/files/{filename} does not require any run-ownership check — any authenticated dashboard user can download any run_id if they know it. Fine for a single-tenant dashboard, but flagging for future multi-tenant hardening.

PrintoutLabelsPage.js LastRunDownloads receives `run` from either analytics.latest_run OR the freshly-returned process() payload; the process payload does NOT include `input_files_count` / `total_files`, so immediately after a fresh upload the 'Files' stat renders as '—' until loadAll() finishes and analytics.latest_run takes over. Suggest passing `total_files: runResult.total_files` in the runResult branch (line 656-664) so the number appears immediately.
